controls_verified: HMAC-authentic terminals with a wrong reason, reason digest, resource, request ID, non-finite time, extra field, action, combat ID, status, or disposition have no terminal effect.
The selected disposition and normalized reason are bound to the exact human-approved resource.
Process-monotonic expiry cannot be revived by wall-clock rollback.
Restart invalidates the old process challenge and produces a distinct nonce/counter resource; the old decision is rejected.
Two concurrent consumers of one live challenge yield exactly one success.
Journal-only or protected-anchor-only deletion remains fail-closed.

residuals.title: Paired journal and protected-anchor deletion or rollback is treated as first installation
residuals.evidence: With an authenticated mutation-started orphan pending, deleting both the journal and protected anchor, or restoring both to their pre-action empty snapshot, made a new instance reconcile successfully with mutation_blocked=false, pending=false, and health=100 while the journal signing key remained unchanged.

exploitability_boundary: The bypass requires delete/restore access to both the protected current-user anchor state and the action journal. It does not require the journal HMAC key or a human authorization decision. This is outside an unprivileged attacker boundary but inside the requested elevated local-state/snapshot adversary.
recommendation: Never infer first installation solely from an empty journal and missing anchor. Retain an independent installation/key-birth witness and fail closed when an established installation loses its anchor; bind the latest sequence to TPM NV or an external append-only witness for rollback resistance, and explicitly cap assurance when neither is configured.

controls_verified: Deleting cursor, high-water, and protected anchor together changes the install epoch/challenge; the old approval is rejected and health remains 45.
One-sided rollback, malformed or truncated high-water state, and static multi-link cursor objects remain fail-incomplete.
A replacement during durable enrollment is detected by the post-commit identity sample.
A replacement immediately after the final sample is detected and replayed on the next poll rather than surviving restart indefinitely.

residuals.title: Lossy event-record identity permits deterministic replacement collisions
residuals.evidence: Changing only content after character 4096 of a StringInserts value, or changing only insert 65, preserved _record_anchor and the retained-channel digest. Restart emitted zero records, retained an empty gap, and reported health 100.

residuals.title: Protected anchor plus cursor/high-water/channel snapshot rollback is accepted
residuals.evidence: Restoring all three authenticated local state objects and the matching older channel snapshot while leaving the stable signing key unchanged loaded bookmark 5 with emitted=[], gap='', health=100. This is the remediation's disclosed software-only rollback boundary.

residuals.title: Live cursor/high-water loss remains green until restart
residuals.evidence: After deleting both durable files, an unchanged poll and then a poll that consumed record 4 both reported health 100. The recreated high-water began from a non-genesis in-memory tail; restart rejected it, reported health 45, and replayed records 1-4.

residuals.title: Concurrent module writers can return success over an invalid durable chain
residuals.evidence: Two listeners synchronized at high-water append produced one ok=true health-100 enrollment and one failure, but restart rejected the resulting high-water authentication and replayed records 1-4 at health 45. The suite-level OS singleton reduces normal production reachability.

exploitability_boundary: The permanent record-identity bypass requires privileged Security-channel replacement but no SHA-256 break or cursor-key access. Protected snapshot rollback requires restoring the protected anchor as well as adjacent files/channel. Live durability loss requires local state deletion. The multi-writer case is mitigated by the application singleton but remains reachable to duplicate in-process or embedded owners.
recommendation: Hash a canonical length-delimited representation of every complete consumed event field and fail incomplete on budget overflow; verify exact durable cursor/high-water objects even on the no-change path; refuse a missing non-genesis high-water; re-read the completed transaction before success; add a state-root-scoped OS writer lease; use TPM or external monotonic witnessing for protected-store rollback claims.
